title: Fix install.sh so a new terminal finds forgel-code on PATH
request: The installer currently completes while the launcher directory never reaches PATH in a freshly opened terminal. It picks the profile file from $SHELL alone: on macOS a bash login shell never reads ~/.bashrc, and under `curl … | sh` $SHELL can be empty, sending the block to ~/.profile while the terminal reads ~/.zshrc. It also never checks that its own change took effect. This change makes the installer detect the real login shell, write the block into a profile file a new terminal actually reads, start a clean login shell afterwards and verify that `forgel-code` resolves, and fail with a message naming the edited file and the observed PATH when it does not. --uninstall removes the block from every profile file the installer can have written.

audit.summary: The release delivers the requested installer behaviour and its follow-up audits: login-shell detection ($SHELL, then invoking process, then account login shell, then /bin/sh), per-shell profile selection (zsh ~/.zshrc; bash first existing of ~/.bash_profile/.bash_login/.profile or a created ~/.bash_profile; POSIX ~/.profile with a warning), a guarded, byte-stable, idempotent marked block, bounded fresh-login-shell verification that only reports success when `command -v forgel-code` equals the newly written launcher and otherwise fails non-zero naming the file, block, shell and observed PATH, and `--uninstall` that strips the block from every candidate profile (.zshrc, .zprofile, .zshenv, .bash_profile, .bash_login, .profile, .bashrc) plus FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE without creating or altering other lines. README and CHANGELOG were updated to match, the earlier v0.1.0 URL and 120-second runtime claim were removed, and the recorded suite runs complete with 218 tests passing. No blocking defect was found; remaining items are non-blocking hardening/cleanup observations.

findings.issue: When /dev/urandom or od is unavailable, random_token falls back to `$$$$$$`, making the private `forgel-code-check` directory name predictable under a shared ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}; another local user could pre-create or guess the path (the mkdir -m 700 retry mitigates but does not remove the predictability).
findings.suggestion: Fail closed (diagnose and abort the check) or derive the token from another non-predictable source instead of the PID when /dev/urandom and od are unavailable, and keep the owner-only mkdir check.

findings.issue: On the success path bounded_run reaps the watchdog but leaves CHECK_WATCHER set, so cleanup_check sends TERM to an already-reaped PID; if the PID were reused in that window an unrelated process could be signalled.
findings.suggestion: Clear CHECK_WATCHER after the successful wait in bounded_run before cleanup_check runs, or have cleanup_check skip signalling when the watcher has already been reaped.

findings.issue: The CHANGELOG [Unreleased] 'Changed' entry describes volatile implementation detail of the test suite ('one read-only checkout copy and one prepared installation per scenario group... configure a limit below the product default'), which D-109 asks documentation not to carry.
findings.suggestion: Reword the entry to state the outcome (a faster suite with unchanged coverage) without internal test structure or limit/timing detail.
